root_cause.text: The `mtd_parser_tplink_safeloader_parse` function in the TP-Link SafeLoader MTD partition parser fails to release the dynamically allocated buffer `buf` on its error cleanup path (`err_free`) when a partition name allocation fails.
root_cause.evidence: The patch diff shows that `kfree(buf)` was added to the `err_free` label in `drivers/mtd/parsers/tplink_safeloader.c` to prevent a memory leak when jumping to this label after a failed allocation of `parts[idx].name`.

bic_trace_step.reason: In the function `mtd_parser_tplink_safeloader_parse`, the buffer `buf` is allocated on line 91 via `mtd_parser_tplink_safeloader_read_table`. If the partition name allocation fails on line 103, the code jumps to the `err_free` label on line 105. However, the error cleanup path at `err_free` (lines 118-121) only frees the previously allocated partition names and does not release `buf` (or the `parts` array itself), leading to a memory leak.
